why_included: Tracks early-stage startup context and monthly operating review needs
research_backing: BLS Business Employment Dynamics tracks establishment age, survival, births, deaths, and startup employment patterns.

why_included: Shows customer traction and whether the company is growing or shrinking
research_backing: Startup success/failure research identifies business development, market fit, customer acquisition, and financial performance as important startup outcome factors.

why_included: Shows whether the startup has enough money to keep operating
research_backing: Startup failure research repeatedly identifies lack of capital, financial problems, and running out of cash as major failure drivers.

why_included: Converts cash and burn into months of operating life
research_backing: Runway uses the direct business formula cash balance divided by monthly burn; cash availability is supported by startup failure research.

why_included: Shows whether customers are leaving and whether revenue quality is weak
research_backing: Startup failure research highlights product-market misfit, weak customer demand, few customers, and customer-service gaps as risk factors.

why_included: Shows whether customer acquisition is too expensive or too slow to recover
research_backing: Startup failure research identifies lack of business development, customer acquisition problems, bad promotion, and weak business models as common risks.

why_included: Adds a customer reaction signal before revenue decline appears
research_backing: NPS research is mixed, so SHARF uses NPS as one small customer sentiment signal rather than a stand-alone predictor.

why_included: Represents whether the team has enough capacity to execute
research_backing: Startup failure literature identifies team, product, business, and market problems as major early-stage failure dimensions; BLS supports tracking startup employment patterns.

why_included: Represents governance and decision support for founders
research_backing: Fundraising and venture research shows startup outcomes depend on multiple factors including stage, networks, and external credibility.

why_included: Represents external financing and economic pressure
research_backing: FRED provides macroeconomic interest-rate series such as FEDFUNDS; SHARF uses a synthetic macro stress proxy for prototype testing.

why_included: Combines multiple risk indicators into one transparent score
research_backing: Startup prediction research supports multi-feature modeling rather than relying on one metric alone.

why_included: Turns numeric score into simple founder-facing category
research_backing: Decision-support outputs are easier to use when numeric scores are translated into action-oriented categories; SHARF uses these as prototype categories.

why_included: Shows future risk as probability instead of one exact prediction
research_backing: Startup outcomes are uncertain; simulation and multi-feature portfolio modeling are appropriate for uncertainty-aware decision support.
